findings.reason: the in-flight case is the one §32 makes routine, and the node as written can close while a resume during a promotion still ends silently, which is the exact loss the section exists to prevent.
findings.text: §31's Deliverable requires that "a resume of a run that has already been promoted, or that is being promoted, is refused with a non-zero exit naming the promotion and its commit", but the done-when's only resume case is "a resume of a run already promoted exits non-zero, and its output names the promotion commit"; a resume issued while a promotion is in flight is never planted, so an implementation that guards only the terminal promoted state passes the gate

findings.reason: the landing caller is the third of three named callers and would remain a coordinator-turn wait; the gate would certify an endpoint the section does not deliver.
findings.text: §32's Deliverable says "A coordinator's `crew complete`, a sweep's acceptance and a landing each request the promotion and return without waiting for it to finish", but the done-when plants only a `crew complete` caller and a sweep pass; no case exercises the landing path, so a node that makes completion and acceptance asynchronous while leaving a landing blocked on its own promotion passes every case

findings.reason: the section's whole point is that the row must not claim liveness it never checked, and the unqueryable case is the one that reproduces that failure.
findings.text: §30's Deliverable separates three scheduler outcomes — any job alive, "asked and listed none", and "When it could not be asked, or the wait names no job, the row says the scheduler was not consulted" — but the done-when plants only the first two and the names-no-job half of the third; no case makes the scheduler unqueryable, so an implementation that reads a failed scheduler query as "listed none" (and again asserts that no job is alive without having looked) passes the gate

findings.reason: a worker following the path either wastes its turn looking for a module that does not exist or creates a parallel `resume.py` beside `resumption.py`, which is the duplicate-implementation hazard the naming rules exist to stop; the path should name `reckon/crew/resumption.py`.
findings.text: §31's Write paths name `reckon/crew/resume.py`, which resolves to nothing: `git log --all -- reckon/crew/resume.py` returns no commit and the resume implementation lives in `reckon/crew/resumption.py` (`_resume`, `mark_resume_launching`) reached through `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §31's write paths name `reckon/crew/resume.py`, which resolves to no file in the repository or its history; the resume path lives in `reckon/crew/resumption.py`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §31's deliverable names two resume-refusal states ("already been promoted, or that is being promoted") and its done-when exercises only the already-promoted one, and §32's deliverable names three callers that must return without waiting while its done-when exercises two.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §30, §31 and §32 each commit the section's evidence fragment, and `docs/evidence/fragments/` exists as the durable home for those fragments (the plan-level record is `docs/evidence/archive/work-flows-to-the-lane-landed.html`, plan.html:96).
rubric_items.naming: pass — the three new test filenames are named by what they assert (`test_a_wait_on_scheduler_jobs_is_not_abandoned.py`, `test_a_coordinator_holds_a_delivered_run.py`, `test_no_caller_waits_on_a_promotion.py`), and no plan label, ticket number or stage name appears in the changed units.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §32's Why is sound and its cited evidence resolves, but §30's deliverable states three distinct scheduler states while its done-when plants only two, and §31's stated root cause (a promotion deletes the pointer and the resume then ends silently) is supported but its deliverable's second state is untested as recorded above.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §30, §31 and §32 states one endpoint (a scheduler-backed wait is not read abandoned; a delivered run can be held and a resume never vanishes; no caller waits on a promotion); none carries two independently closable deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the only open followup, f-wftl-009 (plan.html:242-245), names exactly the five sections not declared `done` (§9, §22, §30, §31, §32), its recommended invocation names §32 which is unbuilt, and `plan-section-depends-on` (plan.html:22) declares only s3/s9/s22, whose targets all resolve and are landed where required.
